subject: physics_2
question_text: Define NAND & NOR gates. Give their truth table.

mark_split.label: Truth table of the NAND gate
Truth table of the NOR gate

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two symbol figures carry 0 marks because the question does not ask for a diagram; they are drawn because a gate is recognised by its symbol. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. PRINTED ERRORS CORRECTED (book p.56): under the NOR gate the book reprints the caption 'Combination of AND Gate with NOT Gate' from the NAND page, and labels the NOR symbol's output 'Y = A.B' with a bar. Both belong to the NAND gate. A NOR gate is an OR gate followed by a NOT gate and its output is the complement of A + B. The book's NOR truth table itself is correct (1, 0, 0, 0). Truth tables hand-checked row by row against both definitions. Overbars are authored as KaTeX because Unicode does not encode them honestly.

recall_prompt: Define the NAND gate and give its four rows, then do the same for the NOR gate.

steps.label: NAND gate
lines: A NAND gate is an AND gate followed by a
NOT gate. It has two input terminals and
Its output is 0 only when both inputs
steps.margin_note: First mark. 'AND gate plus NOT gate' and the output expression with the bar.
steps.why: Every property of the gate follows from the words AND followed by NOT: the expression carries a bar over A · B, the symbol is the AND shape with a bubble, and the output column is the AND column inverted.
common_mistakes: Writing Y = A · B without the bar. That is the AND gate.
Calling it an OR gate followed by NOT. That is the NOR gate.

recall.must_convey: That a NAND gate is an AND gate followed by a NOT gate, with output the complement of A · B.
accept: AND gate followed by a NOT gate
Y equals bar of A dot B
output is zero only when both inputs are one
reject: OR gate followed by a NOT gate

steps.memory_tip: N-AND: read the name backwards — AND first, then the N for NOT.

steps.label: NAND symbol
steps.margin_note: The AND shape — flat back, round nose — with a small circle on the output. The circle is the NOT part.
steps.why: The small circle at the output is the whole difference between the AND symbol and the NAND symbol, so a student who draws the shape but forgets the circle has drawn the wrong gate.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the small circle at the output. Without it the drawing is an AND gate.
Drawing a curved back. The AND shape has a straight back; the curved back belongs to OR.

recall.must_convey: That the NAND symbol is the AND shape with a small circle on the output.
accept: D shape with a circle at the output
draw the AND symbol and add the small circle
reject: curved back with a pointed nose

steps.memory_tip: The bubble means NOT. AND shape plus bubble is NAND.

steps.label: NAND truth table
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Only the last row gives 0.
steps.why: Take the AND column 0, 0, 0, 1 and invert every entry. That is faster than working out four rows separately, and it cannot go wrong if the definition is remembered.
common_mistakes: Writing the AND column 0, 0, 0, 1 by mistake.
Missing a row. All four input pairs must appear.

recall.must_convey: That the NAND output is 1, 1, 1, 0 for the four input pairs.
accept: zero only when both inputs are one
high for the first three rows

steps.label: NOR gate
lines: A NOR gate is an OR gate followed by a
NOT gate. It has two input terminals and
Its output is 1 only when both inputs
steps.margin_note: Third mark. OR plus NOT, and the bar goes over A + B, not over A · B.
steps.why: The book's page 56 repeats the NAND caption and the NAND expression under the NOR gate. Reading the name — NOR is NOT-OR — gives the correct expression every time and catches that misprint.
common_mistakes: Writing the output with a bar over A · B. That is the NAND expression; the book prints it here by mistake.
Calling it an AND gate followed by NOT, which is what the book's caption says here.

recall.must_convey: That a NOR gate is an OR gate followed by a NOT gate, with output the complement of A + B.
accept: OR gate followed by a NOT gate
Y equals bar of A plus B
output is one only when both inputs are zero
reject: AND gate followed by a NOT gate

steps.memory_tip: N-OR: OR first, then the N for NOT.

steps.label: NOR symbol
steps.margin_note: The OR shape — curved back, pointed nose — with a small circle on the output.
steps.why: The two symbols differ only in the back and the nose: the AND shape has a straight back and a round nose, the OR shape a curved back and a pointed nose. Both take the same small circle for NOT.
common_mistakes: Drawing the AND shape with a bubble. That is NAND, not NOR.
Leaving out the small circle at the output. Without it the drawing is an OR gate.

recall.must_convey: That the NOR symbol is the OR shape with a small circle on the output.
accept: curved back and pointed nose with a circle
draw the OR symbol and add the small circle
reject: flat back with a round nose

steps.memory_tip: Curved back = OR. Add the bubble and it is NOR.

steps.label: NOR truth table
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Only the first row gives 1.
steps.why: Take the OR column 0, 1, 1, 1 and invert every entry. The NOR column is the exact opposite of the NAND column, which is a useful check: three zeros here against three ones there.
common_mistakes: Copying the NAND column 1, 1, 1, 0. The NOR column is 1, 0, 0, 0.
Writing the OR column 0, 1, 1, 1 without inverting it.

recall.must_convey: That the NOR output is 1, 0, 0, 0 for the four input pairs.
accept: one only when both inputs are zero
high only for the first row

steps.memory_tip: One one then three zeros — the mirror image of the NAND column.

insider_note: Watch the book here: on page 56 it repeats the NAND caption and the NAND expression under the NOR gate. NOR is OR followed by NOT, and its output is the complement of A + B.
